headlines.headline: CoreWeave struggling to keep up with demand for Nvidia chips, CEO says
headlines.summary: CoreWeave strikes a very bullish tone on demand.
headlines.body:
SAN FRANCISCO, Calif. — What's good for Nvidia ( NVDA ) looks to be good for its key partner in the AI infrastructure boom, CoreWeave ( CRWV ).

"We are struggling to meet demand every day," CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told Yahoo Finance from the Goldman Sachs Communacopia & Tech Conference (video above). "Every GPU we have could be sold to multiple different clients. It is a unique moment, and it continues to be."

Nvidia serves as the backbone, primary supplier, and main financial guarantor for CoreWeave's ever-expansive neocloud operation.

Beyond supplying 100% of the advanced GPUs powering CoreWeave's specialized AI data centers, Nvidia acts as a major strategic shareholder, holding an 11.5% equity stake.

Nvidia said after reporting its fiscal second quarter earnings that it sees 70% revenue growth for fiscal year 2028, above analyst forecasts for 45% growth. The sales gain would be larger — think in excess of 100% — if not for memory chip shortages , Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said.

CoreWeave reported that second quarter sales surged 112% year over year. Adjusted operating profits more than doubled to $1.5 billion.

Driven by explosive enterprise demand for graphics processing unit (GPU) compute and a massive $104 billion total revenue backlog, management raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $12.4 billion to $13.2 billion.

"The quarter demonstrated AI demand remains robust, strengthening pricing power (25% increases across SKUs), growing software/token business, and upside surprises on margins," Citi analyst Tyler Radke wrote. "Overall, this was one of the cleaner quarters we've seen from CoreWeave since the IPO and we think shares should move meaningfully higher on increased investor confidence in the execution and improving profitability."

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team. Follow Sozzi on X @BrianSozzi , Instagram , and LinkedIn . Tips on stories? Email brian.sozzi@yahoofinance.com.

headlines.headline: Nvidia Falls as Its Firmus Bet Lands OpenAI
headlines.summary: The Malaysian agreement validates Nvidia's infrastructure ecosystem, but the chipmaker's direct economics remain undisclosed.
headlines.body:
Nvidia-backed Firmus secured a multiyear agreement to provide OpenAI with computing capacity from two Malaysian data centers. Nvidia ( NASDAQ:NVDA ), the AI-accelerator powerhouse supplying Firmus's next-generation infrastructure, fell approximately 1.5% to $226.86 in Tuesday morning trading.

The OpenAI deal pushes Firmus's committed customer capacity beyond 900 megawatts. The company currently operates two facilities and is building five more across the Asia-Pacific region, with future sites set to deploy Nvidia's Vera Rubin processors at scale. Firmus did not reveal the contract's financial terms, leaving investors without a clear measure of how much hardware demand the agreement could generate.

Nvidia ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) produced $89 billion in data-center revenue last quarter, accounting for roughly 92.5% of total sales. The GuruFocus chart reinforces the company's exceptional profitability and growth, alongside strong financial strength and healthy momentum, while GF Value remains the obvious weak spot. Firmus expands Nvidia's reach into another major AI-infrastructure project, but 900 megawatts measures power capacitynot Nvidia revenueso the real prize will depend on processor volumes, deployment timing and the economics behind the partnership.
